lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: > Do not say that Section $4$ makes all eight norms a blanket rule for every moment of private life.
lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.note: The rewrite now includes the required General Information trap section; Speed Tricks & Shortcuts is optional.

lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: 2. **Professionalism:** Do public work with skill, care, and dedication. Officials should also avoid making public service look like a source of special favors.
lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.note: The dense statutory wording was replaced with short plain-language descriptions of the norms.

lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: Section $4$ gives eight norms of conduct. These are standards for public officials and employees while they carry out official duties.
lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.note: The rewrite now limits the Section 4 norms to the official-duty setting instead of saying they apply at all times.

lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: Republic Act No. $6713$ is the **Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees**. It was approved on February $20$, $1989$ and took effect on March $25$, $1989$.
lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.note: The statute number and all date numerals in this passage are now wrapped in inline math.

lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: How many norms of conduct are listed in Section $4$ of RA $6713$?
lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.note: The example now asks the count directly instead of using meta review-question framing.

lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: **Public accountability** means officials must answer to the people for how they use public power and resources.
lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.note: Public accountability now receives a plain meaning before the lesson relies on it.

lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: Section $4$ frames the eight norms as standards of personal conduct in carrying out official duties. Some individual norms also use broader wording, but the Section $4$ list itself has this official-duty setting.
lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.note: The official-duty applicability boundary is now stated and reinforced in the trap section.

general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.quote: Republic Act No. $6713$ is the **Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees**. It was approved on February $20$, $1989$ and took effect on March $25$, $1989$.
general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.note: The code title and both dates are stated directly as orientation facts, with no invented date-interval calculation.

general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.quote: A supervisor tells an employee to deny a lawful service to a poor applicant because the applicant criticized the office. The employee knows the applicant has the same right to the service as everyone else. Which norm most directly requires fair treatment?
general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.note: A worked rights-versus-duty case now asks the learner to choose the norm requiring fair treatment.

general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.quote: Responsiveness also covers prompt and adequate service, openness of information when allowed, consultation when appropriate, suggestions, simpler procedures, and avoiding red tape.
general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.note: The rewrite now teaches openness, consultation, suggestions, simpler procedures, and red-tape avoidance beyond clear wording alone.

general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.quote: 6. **Nationalism and patriotism:** Be loyal to the Republic and the Filipino people. Support local goods, resources, and technology, and take pride in the country. **Sovereignty** means the Philippines has the right to control its own affairs, and officials should help protect that right from outside control.
general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.note: Nationalism and patriotism now develops local goods, resources, technology, national pride, and sovereignty.

general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.quote: An agency can use suitable locally produced technology for a project and chooses it while meeting the project's needs. The same agency also refuses a foreign demand that would weaken Philippine control over an official matter. Which norm best connects these actions?
general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.note: The rewrite now connects loyalty to the Republic with local resources and protection of Philippine control in an applied case.

general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.quote: The norms do not all describe the same kind of conduct. On an exam, focus on the action in the situation and match it to the norm that most directly covers that action.
general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.note: The lesson now teaches matching conduct to the most direct norm and supplies separate behavior cases for all eight norms.

general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.quote: Section $6$ creates an annual system of incentives and rewards for outstanding public officials and employees. A Committee on Awards reviews performance and gives recognition based on the standards in the law.
general-information-code-of-conduct-ra-6.note: Section 6 is now taught as an annual incentives-and-rewards system, with the awards committee and reward types described.

lesson-code-of-conduct-ra-6713-norms-of-.quote: The norms do not all describe the same kind of conduct. On an exam, focus on the action in the situation and match it to the norm that most directly covers that action.
